definition: In historical psychology and aesthetics, congruence refers to the agreement among parts of a whole. It stresses that nothing is out of place more than it stresses the presence of positively complementary elements.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Congruity; pinned source text

reasons: The definition claims it applies to “historical psychology and aesthetics,” but the packet only defines the term as a property of agreement among parts of an “aesthetic whole,” without mentioning historical psychology specifically.

The definition’s phrasing “nothing is out of place” is not stated in the packet; the packet instead contrasts emphasis on “the mere absence of the inappropriate” versus “relatively less emphasis upon the presence of factors mutually complementary.”
The definition uses “positively complementary elements,” while the packet specifies “factors mutually complementary” (it does not include the qualifier “positively”).
